spec_family.name: Exterior Porch Floor Repaint
spec_family.description: Condition-dependent repaint of existing exterior porch, portico, and covered patio floor surfaces. Dual-substrate spec covering previously-painted concrete and wood tongue-and-groove porch floors. Assessment-first workflow: existing coating condition rating, coating type identification, substrate-specific moisture checks. Existing coating condition (sound/worn/failing/peeling) is the primary RP dimension driving prep intensity — foot traffic wear is the dominant repaint driver on walking surfaces. Porch enamel (acrylic porch & floor paint) is the universal RP finish product regardless of original coating system (coating_system is NOT a dimension — RP converges on single product). Concrete RP prep uses chemical degloss or mechanical abrasion (NO acid etch on RP). Wood RP prep uses scuff sand or scrape/feather. Spot prime for failing (bare patches), full prime for peeling (>30% bare), bonding primer for incompatible existing coatings. Anti-slip aggregate broadcast mandatory on all coats. Steps are conditional scope component (brush only, alternating-step pattern). QT2 (economy single coat refresh) and QT3 (standard 2-coat full repaint). Cure time communication critical — 48-72hr before foot traffic. Uses SF as primary UOM. No height modifier — ground-level work. 35 tasks across 8 modules.

includes: Existing coating condition assessment (sound/worn/failing/peeling) with tape-pull adhesion test
Existing coating type identification (porch enamel, concrete stain, acrylic sealer, unknown)
Concrete moisture assessment via plastic sheet test (ASTM D4263) — conditional on peeling pattern
Wood moisture content verification (MC <15%) via pin-type meter
Chemical degloss for sound/worn concrete (liquid sander/deglosser)
Scuff sand for sound/worn wood (120-150 grit)
Scrape loose/failing paint — concrete and wood
Feather-edge sand at scrape boundaries (80-grit)
Concrete crack fill (hairline to 1/4")
Wood T&G gap fill with exterior wood filler
Spot prime bare areas (failing condition)
Full prime coat (peeling condition — >30% bare substrate)
Bonding primer for incompatible/unknown existing coatings
Porch & floor enamel application — 2 coats QT3, 1 coat QT2 (brush_roll or spray_backroll)
Anti-slip silica sand broadcast into wet coat 1 (field)
Anti-slip aluminum oxide broadcast on steps
Step/riser painting — brush, alternating-step pattern (conditional on steps present)
Edge cut-in at wall base, railing bases, thresholds, expansion joints
Wall base, railing base, door threshold, landscape, hardscape protection
Furniture removal, staging, and return (return may be separate visit after 48-72hr cure)
Final inspection and touch-up
Customer cure-time communication (written schedule)
Tool and equipment cleanup

configuration_dimensions.description: QT2 = economy single-coat refresh on sound existing. QT3 = standard 2-coat full repaint. Porch floor is utilitarian — QT4/QT5 not applicable.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2 valid only for sound existing coating in good condition — touch-up refresh. QT3 is standard full repaint with proper prep.

configuration_dimensions.description: RP-SPECIFIC PRIMARY DIMENSION — drives prep intensity, primer strategy, and labor multiplier. Foot traffic wear is the dominant repaint driver.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Sound = intact, light degloss/scuff. Worn = traffic wear-through in paths, moderate prep. Failing = adhesion loss in patches, scrape + spot prime. Peeling = sheet delamination (often moisture-driven), heavy scrape + full prime.

configuration_dimensions.description: Porch floor substrate material. Drives completely different prep modules.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Concrete = previously-painted concrete slab. Wood = tongue-and-groove porch floor (fir, pine, PT pine). Each substrate has its own prep module.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: brush_roll = roller for field + brush for edges (primary, <400 SF). spray_backroll = airless spray + immediate backroll (2-person crew, >400 SF). Spray-only PROHIBITED on horizontal surfaces.

paintable_items.name: Porch/patio floor field surface
paintable_items.counting_rules: Net porch floor field area in square feet. Measured from PaintScope plan view. Excludes railing footprint and step area.
paintable_items.notes: SF-based. Primary walking surface. Always active. Both concrete and wood substrates.

paintable_items.name: Porch step (tread + riser per step)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count of porch steps. Each tread + riser = 1 unit. Count from PaintScope step metadata.
paintable_items.notes: EA-based. Conditional on steps present. Brush only — roller cannot reach riser face. Alternating-step pattern for access during cure.

valid_input_states.notes: 5 repaint input states. SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN/SEMIGLOSS/FLAT = sound/worn existing porch enamel. SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT = adhesion loss in patches. SS_EXT_PEELING = sheet delamination. SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD/BARE_MASONRY excluded — bare substrate enters via NC spec.

output_state.notes: All RP converges to satin porch enamel output. Single sheen — no variation.

protection_zones_required.notes: Tape + 6" paper at wall-to-floor junction. Always required — porch always abuts house wall on at least one side.
Tape and paper collar at railing post bases. Conditional on railing presence.
Tape + paper/plastic over threshold surface. High-visibility detail.
Drop cloth along porch perimeter where landscape beds are adjacent.
Tape + canvas at hardscape transition. Upgraded to full cover for spray.
Porch furniture staged to off-porch location. Return after 48-72hr cure.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Exterior Primer — Spot/Full
material_systems.notes: Spot prime on failing (bare patches), full prime on peeling (>30% bare). Both concrete and wood.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Incompatible Existing
material_systems.notes: RP-SPECIFIC. Adhesion bridge for unknown/incompatible existing coatings.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Porch & Floor Enamel
material_systems.notes: Universal RP finish. 2 coats at QT3, 1 coat at QT2. Anti-slip aggregate broadcast into wet coat 1.

modules.notes: Wall base, railing, threshold, landscape, hardscape masking
RP-SPECIFIC: condition assessment, coating ID, moisture test (concrete), MC test (wood)
Degloss, scrape, feather sand, crack fill, clean
Scuff sand, scrape, feather sand, wood fill, clean
Cut-in + field (roll or spray) + anti-slip + steps, x2 coats for QT3
Inspect, teardown, furniture return, customer comm, tool cleanup

factor_modifiers.notes: PREP tasks only (scrape + feather sand). RP-SPECIFIC.
Prime and apply tasks. Wood T&G joint detail slows effective rate.

production_summary.stacking_notes: Worst case: peeling (2.00) x wood (1.10) = 2.20x. Well under cap. Modifiers do not actually compound on the same tasks — condition affects scrape, substrate affects apply.

compatibility_rules.title: Wood moisture content hard stop
compatibility_rules.rule: MC must be <15% before porch enamel application. MC >=15% is HARD STOP.

compatibility_rules.title: Concrete moisture migration hard stop
compatibility_rules.rule: Active moisture migration through concrete slab causes coating delamination regardless of prep quality. Peeling pattern consistent with upward moisture = HARD STOP.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: TSK_PFRP_MOISTURE_TEST_CONCRETE mandatory when peeling on concrete.

compatibility_rules.title: Polyurea/epoxy existing coating excluded
compatibility_rules.rule: Existing polyurea or epoxy coatings are outside standard RP scope. Proprietary products require specialty contractor.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: TSK_PFRP_ASSESS_COATING_ID identifies coating type. Polyurea/epoxy = STOP.

compatibility_rules.title: Unknown existing coating requires bonding primer
compatibility_rules.rule: When existing coating type cannot be identified, treat as incompatible. Bonding primer (SYS_EXT_PFRP_PRIMER_BONDING) mandatory before porch enamel.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: TSK_PFRP_ASSESS_COATING_ID determines type. Unknown = bonding primer.

compatibility_rules.title: Anti-slip aggregate mandatory on all horizontal walking surfaces
compatibility_rules.rule: Anti-slip aggregate broadcast into wet coat is mandatory for all porch floor RP. Safety requirement — ANSI DCOF >=0.55.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: TSK_PFRP_ANTI_SLIP_FIELD always active. Aluminum oxide on steps.

compatibility_rules.title: Spray-only prohibited on horizontal surfaces
compatibility_rules.rule: Spray-only application without backroll is PROHIBITED on porch floors. Backroll required for proper film build and aggregate embedment.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: application_method allows only brush_roll and spray_backroll. No spray-only.

compatibility_rules.title: NO acid etch on repaint
compatibility_rules.rule: Acid etching is NC prep for bare concrete. RP uses chemical degloss or mechanical abrasion. Acid etch would damage intact existing coating areas.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: No acid etch tasks in RP prep modules.

compatibility_rules.title: QT2 restricted to sound existing coating only
compatibility_rules.rule: QT2 (single-coat refresh) is only valid on sound existing coating in good condition. Worn, failing, or peeling conditions require QT3 minimum.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: QT2 variants only have applies_when existing_coating_condition = sound.

compatibility_rules.title: Concrete cracks >1/4" outside painting scope
compatibility_rules.rule: Cracks exceeding 1/4" width indicate structural movement — outside painting scope. Flag for concrete contractor.
compatibility_rules.enforcement: TSK_PFRP_CRACK_FILL_CONCRETE limited to hairline-1/4". Larger cracks documented and excluded.

compatibility_rules.title: Cure time communication mandatory
compatibility_rules.rule: Customer must be informed of 48-72hr foot traffic restriction and 7-day heavy furniture restriction. Written schedule provided.

round_configurations.name: QT2 Economy Single Coat — Refresh Only
round_configurations.notes: Single coat porch enamel on sound existing. Anti-slip aggregate in single coat. Economy refresh — customer accepts limitations.

round_configurations.name: QT3 Standard Two Coat — Full Repaint
round_configurations.notes: 2 finish coats. Coat 1 + anti-slip broadcast. Coat 2 encapsulates aggregate. 4-24hr dry between coats. No formal interstage — utilitarian surface.

variants.notes: BASELINE RP. Sound porch enamel on concrete. Chemical degloss + 2 coats enamel. No primer needed. Minimal prep. Most common maintenance repaint.
ECONOMY. Single-coat refresh on sound concrete. Anti-slip in single coat. Touch-up level.
Common residential RP. Worn traffic paths on concrete. Chemical degloss + 2 coats. No primer — existing coating intact at edges/low-traffic areas.
Moderate prep. Scrape failing areas + feather sand + spot prime bare patches + 2 coats enamel.
HIGHEST PREP. Heavy scrape + feather sand + moisture test + full prime + 2 coats. Moisture assessment mandatory — peeling often moisture-driven.
Sound T&G wood porch. Scuff sand + MC verify + 2 coats enamel. No primer. T&G back-brush during rolling.
Worn wood porch — traffic wear at doorway approach. Scuff sand + MC verify + 2 coats. No primer unless bare wood exposed at wear paths.
Failing wood porch. Scrape + feather sand + MC verify + spot prime bare areas + 2 coats enamel.
HIGHEST PREP WOOD. Heavy scrape + feather sand + MC verify + full prime + 2 coats. Peeling on wood often indicates moisture from below.
Large porch spray variant. Chemical degloss + spray + backroll. 2-person crew. Justified for >400 SF porches.
Unknown existing coating triggers bonding primer. Full coat bonding primer + 2 coats enamel regardless of condition.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: House wall at porch floor junction. Protection is THIS spec's responsibility.
Railing post bases at porch floor. Protection (masking) is THIS spec's responsibility. Railing painting is separate spec.
Door threshold at porch-to-interior transition. Critical tape line. Protection is THIS spec's responsibility.
Foundation below porch deck. Not painted in this scope.

risk_flags.title: Moisture migration through concrete slab
risk_flags.description: Porch floors over crawl spaces or slab-on-grade without vapor barrier experience upward moisture migration. This is the #1 cause of porch floor paint peeling. Repainting over active moisture will fail again.
risk_flags.mitigation: Moisture assessment module (TSK_PFRP_MOISTURE_TEST_CONCRETE) triggered on peeling concrete. If positive, HARD STOP — address moisture source before repainting.

risk_flags.title: Unknown existing coating adhesion failure
risk_flags.description: Porch floors with unknown coatings (concrete stain, acrylic sealer) may not accept porch enamel directly. Adhesion failure after RP is expensive callback.
risk_flags.mitigation: Assessment identifies coating type. Unknown = bonding primer mandatory.

risk_flags.title: Customer damage during cure period
risk_flags.description: 48-72hr foot traffic restriction and 7-day furniture restriction create significant customer inconvenience. Premature foot traffic damages coating and ruins anti-slip texture.
risk_flags.mitigation: TSK_PFRP_CUSTOMER_COMM with written schedule. Alternate entry path planning.

risk_flags.title: T&G joint moisture entry on wood porches
risk_flags.description: Tongue-and-groove joints on wood porches allow water entry between boards. Standing water on porch floor wicks into joints and causes rot and paint peeling from within the joint.
risk_flags.mitigation: T&G gap fill in prep. Brush primer and finish into joint grooves. MC test verifies current moisture level.

site_condition_rules.notes: No height modifier — porch floor is ground-level work.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup (mobilize, furniture) -> Protect (wall base, railing, threshold, landscape, hardscape) -> Assess (condition, coating ID, moisture/MC) -> Prep Concrete OR Prep Wood (substrate-dependent) -> Prime (condition-dependent) -> Apply Coat 1 + Anti-Slip -> Dry 4-24hr -> Apply Coat 2 -> Inspect/Touch-Up -> Teardown -> Customer Comm -> Tool Cleanup
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Wall base -> Railing bases -> Thresholds -> Landscape edge -> Hardscape edge -> Furniture staging (done first in setup)
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Cut-in coat 1 -> Field roll/spray coat 1 -> Anti-slip broadcast -> Steps coat 1 -> Dry 4-24hr -> Cut-in coat 2 -> Field coat 2 -> Steps coat 2 -> Final inspect
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO acid etch on RP. NO spray-only (backroll required). NO coating at MC >15%. NO painting over active moisture migration. NO recoating polyurea/epoxy without specialty contractor.

relationships.cross_spec_protection_note: Wall base, railing base, and threshold masking is THIS spec's responsibility.
relationships.notes: First RP spec for porch floor surfaces. Sibling to SF_PORCH_FLOOR_EXT_NC. Key RP additions: assessment module, existing_coating_condition dimension, condition-driven prep modifiers, bonding primer for incompatible coatings, chemical degloss (replaces NC acid etch), moisture assessment on peeling concrete, cure-time communication. Application rates similar to NC — prep is the RP cost driver.

sections_used: Porch enamel as universal RP product

research_corrections.original_claim: Coating system should be a configuration dimension for RP
research_corrections.corrected_to: Coating system is NOT a dimension for RP. All RP uses porch enamel regardless of original coating. Original polyurea/epoxy excluded from RP scope entirely.
research_corrections.source: Field convention — RP converges on single product

research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable — excluded per PaintFactor OS RC-003.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior porch floor repaint. FIRST RP SPEC for porch floor surfaces — sibling to SF_PORCH_FLOOR_EXT_NC. Key features: assessment-first workflow (condition rating, coating ID, substrate-specific moisture checks), existing_coating_condition as primary RP dimension (sound/worn/failing/peeling), single RP finish product (porch enamel satin — coating_system NOT a dimension), dual-substrate (concrete/wood) with substrate-specific prep modules, condition-driven primer strategy (none/spot/full/bonding), chemical degloss for concrete RP (NO acid etch), anti-slip aggregate mandatory, QT2/QT3 range (utilitarian surface), 2 paintable items (floor SF + step EA conditional), 35 tasks across 8 modules (all binary), 3 material systems (acrylic primer + bonding primer + porch enamel), 2 factor modifiers (condition + substrate), 2 round configurations, 6 protection zones, 11 variants, 9 PaintScope inputs. Max modifier stack 2.20x under 4.0x cap. Cure-time communication task for customer impact management.
